answer: A sybil operator can mint keys cheaply, but its clones all look out from the same place: same relays, same timing, same blind spots. So at random intervals each identity must probe a different assigned set of beacons and publish what it saw, latency, order, failures, building a public atlas of independent vantages. Quartz timers in the probes make the signal hard to backdate or replay. Honest maps disagree in ordinary ways; clones' maps correlate almost perfectly, and faking diversity means deploying separate infrastructure for every name, so scale stops being free.
